title: Vector API parity: iterator semantics, error-code normalization, and stream-compat adapter
creator: Marco Nguyen
description:
Problem: Multiple client SDKs and legacy partners rely on varying pagination semantics (cursor tokens, Link headers, page offsets) and different HTTP error mappings from the embeddings + reranker endpoints. Some clients stream results and expect stable iterator semantics; others expect strict per-page idempotency and specific retry hints. This divergence causes production client breakage during runtime rollouts and complicates gateway fallbacks.

Goal: Ship a compatibility layer (adapter) that provides: 1) a stable iterator contract for streaming and non-streaming clients, 2) normalized HTTP error mapping with explicit retry hints/idempotency signals, and 3) a canonical pagination adapter that supports cursor tokens and Link-header style iteration while preserving performance and cacheability. The adapter should be backward-compatible with legacy clients and opt-in for newer clients.

Scope: API layer + gateway mapping + SDK guidance + runtime telemetry. Does NOT include deep changes to model-serving kernels or quantization.

Acceptance Criteria (high level):
- New adapter can translate legacy Link-header pagination into cursor tokens and vice-versa with no functional regressions for 99.9% of historical calls recorded in traffic sample.
- HTTP error mappings published and implemented: 400/422 client errors preserved, 429 includes Retry-After header and an explicit "x-retry-hint" when applicable, 503 mapped to graceful fallback with consistent idempotency metadata.
- Streaming clients receive stable iterator semantics: partial result offsets (start_index) are present for resumability and dedup suppression.
- E2E tests and SDK integration tests added; rollout plan with canary traffic and automated rollback on increased error or latency.

Risks / Trade-offs:
- Additional translation layer could add 5–10ms median latency for small requests; mitigations include lightweight caching and bypass rules for pinned customers.
- Mapping every historical client behavior perfectly is impossible; we will prioritize top 10 partners + top 90% of traffic patterns.

Out-of-scope for this ticket: telemetry retention changes, billing adjustments, and non-vector endpoints.
acceptance_criteria: Adapter translates Link-header pagination to cursor tokens without breaking legacy iterators
Published HTTP->semantic mapping and SDK checks verify headers and retry hints
Streaming responses include stable start_index + dedup id hint for resumability
Automated integration tests cover cursor conversions, Link header parsing, and retry header propagation
Canary rollout plan with metric thresholds (error-rate, tail-latency, consumer-uptime) and rollback playbook
comments: 2025-01-28 Marco Nguyen: Created ticket after incident on 2025-01-24 where two major partners observed duplicate items when switching from Link headers to cursor tokens. Attached incident summary: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INC/2025-01-24-vector-pagination-duplicates

2025-02-03 Lena Ortiz: Scoped initial PoC — gateway adapter that rewrites Link header -> cursor and injects x-retry-hint when 429/503 detected. PoC repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/compat-adapters PR: #2345

2025-02-10 Eng review (SRE): Concern about extra latency for small payloads. Proposal: add route-level bypass for customers with "low-overhead" flag and cache common cursor translations for 60s. See design notes: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1abc-compat-design

2025-02-14 PM note: Prioritize partner compatibility matrix — we will onboard top 6 partners first for the canary. Partner list & special cases: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/partner-compat-matrix

2025-02-18 Design feedback (Aisha Patel): UX in the Console needs to surface pagination mode and retry hints per-route (Dropdown: cursor | link | hybrid). UX spec: https://www.figma.com/file/xxxxx/vector-pagination-adapter

2025-02-21 ENG update (Jorge Silva): Implemented Link header parser and cursor encoder in the gateway. Integration tests added for cursor <-> link conversions. PR #2389 opened for review: https://github.com/redwood-inference/gateway/pull/2389

2025-02-24 Review comment (Security): Verify that cursor encoding does not leak internal shard IDs — recommended using HMAC with per-tenant key. See security note: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/Sec/Cursor-HMAC-Recommendation

2025-02-25 Eng update (Lena Ortiz): Switched to HMAC-encoded cursor tokens and added 'x-idempotency-policy' header to describe retry semantics. Perf tests show +6ms median on small queries; mitigations being tested (cache + bypass). Performance dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/vec/adapter-perf?var=env=canary

2025-02-28 PM decision: Proceed with canary for top partners; default adapter mode = hybrid (preserve Link if client asked for it, otherwise provide cursor). Canary window planned 2025-03-03 -> 2025-03-10

2025-03-01 Eng note (Jorge Silva): Added streaming compatibility support — when streaming is requested, server will emit an initial 'iterator-metadata' JSON chunk that includes start_index and a dedup-token for the connection. SDKs will be updated to resume streams using that token.

2025-03-02 PM update (Marco Nguyen): Drafted rollout playbook and rollback criteria. Playbook: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/PM/Vector-Adapter-Rollout-Playbook; Rollback triggers: error-rate +0.2% absolute, p99 latency +40ms relative, partner-blocking errors >1 per minute.
notes: Related discussions: internal #api-compat on Slack; please ping @platform-team for canary approvals
SDK owners: add transparent cursor/crosswalk helpers in the next SDK release (js/python/java) to ease migration
Follow-up work: formalize per-tenant policy for adapter bypass and billing implications (new ticket to be created)
We will also document streaming iterator metadata and provide a small migration guide for partners that rely on chunked streams.
